definitions.gate: Expected block means a defect with authored error severity. Actual block means exit code 1 on a scored result. Unscored cases remain unavailable, regardless of their process exit code.
definitions.unmatchedFindings: The historical falsePositives counter counts all findings except at most one location match per defect case. It includes duplicate matches.

timing.start: review_diff_at starts its review timer before diff preparation
timing.end: final review envelope construction records elapsed milliseconds
included: diff preparation and review work within the scored invocation
model calls and internal repair/retry work within that invocation
excluded: forge/CI queue time and developer workflow

definitions.scope: Selected source excerpts and output findings, all primary-run case verdicts, and repeated-run output availability. Request prompts, headers and per-attempt accounting are not included.

findings.title: Comment claims fallback to defaults but code throws
findings.body: The added comment states "falls back to defaults when config is missing" but the code on the same line throws the error instead of returning defaultConfig. This is a fabricated claim about behavior. Correct the comment to state that missing config is now a fatal error, or restore the return-defaultConfig behavior if fallback is still intended.

findings.title: Config loader now throws instead of returning defaults
findings.body: The function previously returned defaultConfig on error, guaranteeing callers always received a config object. It now throws, so any caller without a try/catch will crash on missing or invalid config. This is a breaking contract change. If fallback is still required, restore the return-defaultConfig path; otherwise confirm callers handle the exception and remove the misleading comment.

files.content: export const providerClient = createClient({ timeoutMs: 0, retry: retryPolicy.standard() });

docs.content: Provider calls should keep bounded timeouts so workers cannot hang indefinitely.

findings.targetContract: Setting the timeout to zero can leave provider calls unbounded and tie up workers indefinitely.

findings.title: Request timeout disabled by setting timeoutMs to 0
findings.body: The provider client timeout was changed from 5_000 ms to 0, which disables the request timeout in most HTTP client implementations. Hung provider requests can block indefinitely and exhaust connection pools. Restore a finite timeout value, or if zero is intentional for a streaming endpoint, gate it behind an explicit no-timeout option.

findings.title: Metric renamed from provider.request to provider.requests
findings.body: The telemetry metric identifier was changed from 'provider.request' to 'provider.requests', a breaking contract change for any dashboard, alert, or SLO referencing the old name. Existing telemetry consumers will silently stop receiving data. Restore the metric name 'provider.request' or emit both names during a transition period.

findings.title: Accept header content type changed to application/vnd.api+json
findings.body: The Accept header was switched from 'application/json' to 'application/vnd.api+json', requesting a JSON:API content type. Provider endpoints that do not support this content type may return 406 Not Acceptable or a different response format, breaking existing integrations. Restore 'application/json' or confirm every targeted provider supports application/vnd.api+json before merging.

findings.targetContract: The delete path skips the archive table and loses the only recovery copy.

findings.title: Archive replaced with permanent deletion
findings.body: The call changed from archiveFile(fileId) to storage.delete(fileId), replacing a soft-delete/archive with a hard delete. If any caller, restore flow, or audit consumer expects archived files to remain recoverable, this diff introduces irreversible data loss. Verify that storage.delete is the intended contract and that no restore or audit path depends on the archived copy, or keep archiving as the default and gate hard deletion behind an explicit flag.

adjudications.title: Config loader now throws instead of returning defaults
adjudications.explanation: The matched finding and extra warning cite the same return-defaultConfig to throw-err change. Both describe the seeded fallback contract; the warning is not an additional unique defect.

adjudications.title: Metric renamed from provider.request to provider.requests
adjudications.explanation: The rename is present, but the supplied evidence provides no dashboard, alert, SLO, consumer, or metric-name stability contract establishing the asserted breakage.

adjudications.title: Accept header content type changed to application/vnd.api+json
adjudications.explanation: The finding explicitly says endpoints may reject or change their response. No supplied endpoint contract establishes that failure.

representativeExplanations.interpretation: Both models return a warning and allow the gate for the seeded must-block removal of the archive step. This is a false accept under the authored contract, despite detecting the change.
The contract makes a token invalid exactly at expiry. GLM emits no finding and allows the gate; Luna reports the boundary error and blocks it.

The authored timeout risk is advisory. Both models promote it to an error and block, a false block under the benchmark rubric. This does not establish that blocking a disabled timeout is always wrong in production.
GLM returns review/invalidOutput and remains unavailable for quality scoring. Luna emits no finding and allows this seeded must-block unit-conversion defect.
